source.snippet: Brave is as good results as Kagi for me and more anonymity-focused, because your searches aren't tied to an account, but I like that Kagi has a simple business model. I would pay for either if I could pay 3 dollars or less per month with Monero. — HN comment on 'Back to Kagi', captured 2026-07-22.

problem_statement: Privacy-conscious users are willing to pay for private search engines but are blocked from doing so because existing paid options (Kagi) require account-linked payment, undermining the privacy proposition. There is latent demand for a truly anonymous paid search tier.
target_segment: Privacy-focused individual users and developers who actively use tools like Brave, Monero, or VPNs and distrust account-linked subscriptions.
notes: Explicit 'I would pay' signal with a specific price point ($3/mo) and payment method (Monero). The pain is the contradiction between paying for privacy and having to create an account to do so. Opportunity: anonymous prepaid search access (token/voucher model, Monero/crypto payment, no account required). Single HN comment but touches a real structural gap in the privacy-tools market.
